title: Completeness of the strict integral derived quotient limit
statement: For a prime ell, scheme W, simultaneous integral derived reduction I and any total right-derived inverse limit RZ as in [def-sfb-diagonal-system-interface], and any additive coefficient equivalence e from abelian sheaves to modules over the lifted integers, every value e(RZ(I.T(K))) is derived complete for the ideal generated by ell. This is an object property only and asserts no natural augmentation or universal mapping property.

source.place: Tag 099M, lemma-naive-completion, Koszul tower proof; principal orthogonality and pro-isomorphism argument in source Complete/Principal.lean

proof.text: The cokernel projection onto the nth ordinary quotient is epic. Cancel it to deduce that ell^(n+1) times the identity of that quotient is zero. Degreewise this kills the identity of the evaluated quotient complex. Evaluation on towers has an exact left adjoint (finite coproducts indexed by arrows from n), and the adjunction localizes to derived categories. Thus derived evaluation is a right adjoint and preserves the pointwise right Kan extension that defines I.T. The uniqueness part of that Kan extension transports the annihilation identity to the derived evaluated reduction of every K.

Apply the Milnor triangle for the given total right derived inverse limit RZ to I.T(K). Its evaluation functor agrees with localized ordinary evaluation, hence its nth value is killed by ell^(n+1) by the previous step. Map the triangle through the exact coefficient equivalence, which preserves the product cone.

Every map from an ell-invertible object, or any shift of it, to a term killed by a power of ell is zero. The product cone makes every map to the product zero. Exactness of Hom into the Milnor triangle makes every map to its first vertex zero as well. Since ell is a nonzero divisor in the lifted integers, the principal orthogonality criterion proves derived completeness. This works for zero objects, the empty scheme, and unbounded complexes.

lean.statement:
theorem integral_strict_limit_complete (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime] (W : Scheme.{u})
    [HasDerivedCategory.{u + 1} (DiagonalAb W)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{u + 1} (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ DiagonalAb W)]
    (I : DiagonalDerivedReduction ℓ (𝟭 (DiagonalAb W)))
    (RZ : DerivedCategory (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ DiagonalAb W) ⥤ DerivedCategory (DiagonalAb W))
    (ηZ : (lim : (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ DiagonalAb W) ⥤ DiagonalAb W).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ) ⋙
      DerivedCategory.Q ⟶ DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ RZ)
    (hRZ : RZ.IsRightDerivedFunctor ηZ
      (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ DiagonalAb W) (.up ℤ)))
    (e : DiagonalAb W ≌
      Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology W) (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} ℤ)))
    [e.functor.Additive] [e.inverse.Additive] :
    ∀ K : DerivedCategory (DiagonalAb W),
      DerivedCategory.derivedComplete (Scheme.ProEt.topology W)
        (Ideal.span {(ℓ : ULift.{u + 1} ℤ)})
        (((I.T ⋙ RZ) ⋙ e.mapDerivedCategory.functor).obj K)
